# `extension-changed-sdk`

x- extension the policy classifies as sdk changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `sdk` |
| **Default severity** | `info` · `--profile sdk`: `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `extension-changed-sdk` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M6) |
| **Group** | Docs (annotations only) ([RULES.md section 10](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An `x-` extension that the policy's `extensions` section classifies as `sdk` changed, e.g. `x-enum-varnames` or `x-go-type`, which code generators read.

## Why this default

Generated SDK code changes (renamed constants, different types) even though the JSON on the wire is the same. `info` by default, `warn` under `--profile sdk`.

## Example

From test case [`extension-changed-sdk`](../../test/cases/extension-changed-sdk/): The policy classifies x-enum-varnames as sdk: renaming the generated constants is extension-changed-sdk (info; warn under --profile sdk), not a docs change.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
        type: string
        enum: [a, b]
-       x-enum-varnames: [Available, Sold]
+       x-enum-varnames: [IsAvailable, IsSold]
```

Findings:

- `extension-changed-sdk` · info · #/components/schemas/Status

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  extension-changed-sdk: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the extension value, or treat the change as an SDK release with notes.
